Senses.Explanation: mixing (和) mud (泥) and blending (合) water (水): “mixing mud and blending water.” Chan records make the ordinary mixing image an appraisal of sayings, explanations, and speakers. In a recasting of three phrases, "understanding from the first phrase" is called "mixing mud and blending water," followed by "binding oneself without a rope" and "landing with all four edges on the ground" (第一句薦得，和泥合水；第二句薦得，無繩自縛；第三句薦得，四稜著地). Another record groups it with "speaking a dream without a dream" and "not knowing good from bad" (無夢說夢，和泥合水，撒屎撒尿，不識好惡). Yet the phrase also stands as a direct answer to "what is the true source of the great road?" (如何是大道真源), and one discourse pairs "where wind cannot enter" with "mixing mud and blending water" in both directions. Another contrasts failing to mark the moment, when black and white remain undistinguished, with marking it too late, called "mixing mud and blending water." These are different recorded placements of one image. The texts do not supply the uniform gloss “descending to the student's level,” so neither does this entry.
